# package: # Every known survivor of scripts/mutation-baseline.tsv, one row each. The
# score is a scalar and cannot tell a new survivor from an accidental kill
# that leaves the count the same; this file is the second, structural
# key is <file>:<mutator>:<hash16>, where file is the path go-mutesting
# reports (.mutator.originalFilePath, relative to the gate root) and hash16
# is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the diff's hunk body
# (the -/+/space lines, header and @@ lines dropped, joined and trimmed).
# The line number is deliberately NOT part of the key: a line moves when
# code above it moves and the mutant does not.
# The gate turns red two ways: an escaped mutant with no row here (NEW
# SURVIVOR -- something now escapes that this file does not know about),
# or a row here with no matching escaped mutant (STALE ROW -- a test now
# kills what used to survive, and the row is out of date). Both are
# failures for the same reason a stale exclusion fails the predicate table
# in fs: a list that has drifted from the run is worse than no list.
# where is file:line mutator at the time the row was written, for a reader
# only -- the gate never compares it, so it may go stale without harm.
# reason is one sentence, why no test can observe the mutant; a row with an
# empty reason is refused (exit 2), because a survivor nobody read is not
# a survivor anybody can vouch for.
# Rows for ./ , ./role/ and ./goroutine/ were computed from a report captured
# at ee9b2bb and matched to the classes this file's own baseline row names.
# ./crash/'s rows were captured by running the gate itself at ee9b2bb in a
# scratch worktree with an empty list, and matched to the baseline row and to
# the commit that reads its 97 survivors (d2d69f6~1). A row not named by
# either source was read from the function directly when this file was
# written (C5), and is marked UNREAD in that commit's body rather than here,
# since the gate does not read a fifth column.
# observed.go:70's sort.Strings removal escaped one live run and was killed
# by another at the same commit: TestObservedNamesEveryPathTheRecorderServed
# builds exactly two paths, so slices.IsSorted(got) is satisfied about half
# the time by map iteration alone, sort call or not. It is left out of this
# file on purpose -- a row that is itself a coin flip would make the gate's
# own verdict a coin flip, which is worse than the gap it would paper over.
# carry no rows because their baseline floor is 1.00 with zero survivors.
